NVDA.supply_chain_summary: NVIDIA sits at the apex of the AI infrastructure value chain as a fabless semiconductor designer, outsourcing all chip manufacturing to TSMC while supplying the dominant GPU platforms consumed by hyperscalers, cloud providers, and enterprises globally. Its near-monopoly position in AI accelerators (~80%+ market share) creates extreme downstream demand concentration among a handful of large cloud customers, while its upstream dependency on TSMC's advanced packaging and HBM memory suppliers represents its most significant supply chain vulnerability.

AAPL.supply_chain_summary: Apple sits at the apex of a highly complex global supply chain, acting as a 'fabless' designer of proprietary silicon and system integrator that sources specialized components from hundreds of suppliers across Asia, Europe, and North America. Its downstream reach spans carrier partners, enterprise customers, and a high-margin digital services ecosystem (App Store, advertising, licensing) that increasingly diversifies revenue beyond hardware device sales.

MU.supply_chain_summary: Micron Technology sits in the middle of the semiconductor memory supply chain, heavily dependent on a concentrated group of capital equipment suppliers—particularly ASML, AMAT, and Lam Research—for the advanced lithography and etch tools required to manufacture DRAM and NAND at cutting-edge nodes. On the demand side, Micron's revenue is driven by hyperscale cloud providers, AI accelerator manufacturers (especially NVIDIA for HBM), and consumer electronics OEMs, making it highly sensitive to data center capex cycles, AI infrastructure build-outs, and smartphone upgrade trends.

ARM.supply_chain_summary: ARM occupies a uniquely asset-light position at the apex of the semiconductor IP ecosystem, licensing CPU/GPU/NPU architectures to virtually every major chip designer rather than manufacturing silicon itself, making its downstream customer base essentially the entire global semiconductor industry. Its upstream dependencies are primarily software-centric — EDA tools from Cadence and Synopsys — rather than physical materials, giving it an exceptionally high-margin, low-capital-intensity business model with leverage over nearly every connected device on earth.

MRVL.supply_chain_summary: Marvell Technology sits at a critical junction in the data infrastructure semiconductor supply chain, designing fabless SoCs that are manufactured by leading foundries (primarily TSMC) and sold to hyperscale cloud providers, networking OEMs, and telecom equipment makers. Its strategic pivot toward custom AI accelerators (XPUs) and high-speed optical interconnects for AWS, Google, and Microsoft makes it increasingly dependent on a small number of large hyperscaler customers, while its reliance on TSMC for advanced-node fabrication represents a key upstream concentration risk.
